options: The practice of defining a standard, enterprise-wide representation of core data entities so all systems can exchange information consistently
The practice of defining reasoning rules for machines
The practice of arranging concepts into hierarchies
The practice of tuning a database for performance
The practice of writing natural-language fact sentences
questions.explanation: A canonical model establishes a shared, authoritative structure that serves as the common reference point for integration across systems.

questions.stem: What does the term canonical refer to?
questions.explanation: Canonical refers to a standard or accepted form, as in a mathematics representation expressed in a normalised, agreed structure.

questions.stem: What problem arises with point-to-point integration as an enterprise grows?
options: Systems cannot be connected at all
Only one system can send data
The number of integrations expands rapidly, creating tight coupling, duplicated transformation logic and high maintenance overhead
questions.explanation: With point-to-point mappings the integration landscape becomes fragile, with tight coupling, duplicated logic and high maintenance as systems are added.

questions.stem: In a canonical approach, what does each system translate to and from?
questions.explanation: Instead of every system translating to every other system, each system translates only to and from the canonical structure.

questions.stem: If an ERP integrated with twenty applications is replaced under a canonical model, what must be updated?
questions.explanation: Only the ERP-to-canonical mapping changes; the other applications keep communicating with the canonical structure unchanged.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a standardised element of a canonical Loan Application?
questions.explanation: The canonical Loan Application includes Customer Identifier, Application Identifier, Application Date, Loan Amount and Approval Decision.

questions.stem: How does Canonical Data Modelling differ from ontology modelling?
options: Canonical modelling focuses on practical interoperability and exchange; ontology modelling focuses on meaning, classification and reasoning
Canonical modelling enables inference; ontology modelling does not
Ontology modelling is used only at integration layers
Canonical modelling defines hierarchies of concepts
questions.explanation: Canonical modelling's objective is predictable, standardised exchange between heterogeneous systems, not inference or reasoning.

questions.stem: Where are canonical models typically implemented?
options: At integration layers such as APIs, service buses, integration hubs or event-driven architectures
questions.explanation: Canonical models are typically implemented at integration layers such as APIs, service buses, integration hubs or event-driven architectures.

questions.stem: How many mappings does a point-to-point approach require, as expressed in the integration comparison?
questions.explanation: In point-to-point every system translates directly to every other system, giving n × (n-1) mappings; canonical modelling maps each system once.

questions.stem: What kind of integration pattern does Canonical Modelling replace, and with what?
options: It replaces many-to-many integrations with one-to-many
questions.explanation: Canonical Modelling replaces many-to-many spaghetti integrations with one-to-many via a shared hub, a massive reduction in complexity.
